title: php://filter
items: It allows you to access different I/O streams at the application level (standard I/O, memory streams, etc.).
In short, you are telling PHP: <highlight>Before processing this file, modify its content.</highlight>
This is crucial for reading PHP source code, as normal LFI would execute the code instead of displaying it.

text: Let's look at a basic example of Source Code Disclosure.

title: Understanding the Command
items: Here we used <highlight>convert.base64-encode</highlight> so that the PHP file is rendered as a string rather than executed.
The <highlight>resource</highlight> parameter is required; it specifies the stream/file to filter.
If the extension (like .php) is automatically appended by the app, you only need the filename (e.g., 'config' instead of 'config.php').

text: Before extracting source code, you must identify available PHP pages using tools like <highlight>ffuf</highlight> or <highlight>gobuster</highlight>.

title: Pro-Tip for LFI Fuzzing
items: Do not ignore <highlight>301</highlight>, <highlight>302</highlight>, or <highlight>403</highlight> status codes.
Even if a page is forbidden or redirects, an LFI vulnerability might still allow you to read its underlying source code.
Once one file is read, scan it for references to other internal PHP files (like database configs or includes).

title: What is read?
items: <highlight>read=</highlight> tells PHP to apply filters when the file is being read.
If only one filter is used, PHP assumes read mode automatically.
When chaining multiple filters, <highlight>read=</highlight> must be explicitly defined.

text: Now let's look at a chained read filter.

title: Understanding Chained Filters
items: Combined using the <highlight>|</highlight> symbol and applied from left to right.
Useful for bypassing complex WAFs that might flag a simple base64 string but miss a ROT13-encoded base64 string.

title: What is write?
items: <highlight>write=</highlight> applies filters when data is being written to a file.
Requires the application to use functions like <highlight>file_put_contents()</highlight>.
In a normal LFI using include(), <highlight>write=</highlight> does not work because include() only reads.

title: Logic for Writing Shells
items: You supply base64-encoded payload (e.g., a web shell) in a parameter that the app writes to disk.
The filter decodes it on-the-fly, saving the clean PHP code to the target resource.
This bypasses filters that block strings like '<?php system($_GET[0]); ?>' in transit.

text: By mastering these wrappers, you move from just reading system files to disclosing full web application logic and potentially achieving Remote Code Execution.
